newsitem.title: USA: Industry backs FAA airport privatization standards.
newsitem.headline: Industry backs FAA airport privatization standards.

text.p: Airport industry reps lined up at a public hearing Tuesday to comment on Federal Aviation Administration's pilot program for privatizing airports, but bond financing issues did not come up.

Representatives from Airports Council International - North American; National Air Transportation Association; Infrastructure Management Group, Inc. and others generally supported procedures that FAA proposed on April 22 that tell airport owners how to apply for the pilot enacted by the U.S. Congress last year.
Written comments on the draft procedures are due June 4.

Currently, most U.S. airports are operated by cities, counties and other public authorities. But as more localities privatize municipal services to relieve tight budgets, the idea of selling airports to nonpublic entities is gaining steam.
The problem is that private owners would not be eligible for airport development grants under the Airport and Airway Improvement Act of 1982.

So Congress in 1996 set up the pilot program, which would allow private owners to get the U.S. grants as long as they agree to keep the facility as an airport, operate it safely, make it available to the general public and meet other conditions.
But privatization is expected to raise issues about what to do about the existing debt service at airports that are switched to private hands.

"These are some of the questions that have to be answered," Benedict Castellano, manager of FAA's airport safety and compliance branch, said in a telephone interview on Tuesday. "We don't know yet for sure."
"While the city may (continue to) guarantee the bonds, they would expect the new airport owner to pay it off," Castellano ventured.
"Those are things that the bonds people and the chief financial officers of companies and cities would have to work out. A lot of different things can be done," he said.
